llm.summary: This is a coherent workout recording summarizer with disclosed helper scripts and optional network use, but users should notice the dataset cache and cloud transcription behavior.

dimensions.detail: The skill purpose, accepted audio/transcript inputs, summary rules, duration helper, exercise-name matching helper, and optional transcription paths fit a strength-training summary workflow.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The workflow documents local-first handling, save-only-when-asked behavior, API key handling, and dataset matching; the automatic GitHub dataset download is disclosed in the reference workflow but less prominent in the top-level skill text.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The artifact contains markdown instructions and two small Python helpers, with no install hook, dependency installer, autostart mechanism, obfuscation, or privilege escalation.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Reading user-provided workout files, running local helper commands, using ffmpeg/Whisper examples, and optionally calling configured transcription APIs are proportionate, but cloud transcription can send private workout audio to a provider.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No background persistence or elevated privilege behavior appears; the only automatic persistence identified is caching a public exercise dataset under the user's home cache directory, plus output files only when requested or produced by chosen tools.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Install if you are comfortable with a helper that may download and cache a public exercise dataset from GitHub. For private workouts, prefer an existing transcript or local Whisper; only use Groq/OpenAI-style transcription when you are comfortable sending the audio to that provider.
llm.findings:
[LP3] expected: File access, shell helpers, and optional network transcription are expected for summarizing local recordings; the artifacts include local-first guidance and warn not to embed API keys.
[TP4] expected: Dataset standardization is mentioned in the top-level summary rules and documented in the workflow, so the dataset matching behavior is purpose-aligned rather than hidden tool poisoning.
[SDI-1] expected: The helper can fetch and cache a public exercise dataset when no local copy is present; this is a real side effect that could be clearer at runtime, but it supports exercise-name standardization and does not send user workout data.
[SDI-2] expected: The hardcoded URL points to a public GitHub raw exercise dataset used as reference data; it creates a supply-chain dependency but is not unrelated or deceptive behavior.
[SQP-2] expected: The cache write under ~/.cache is a transparency concern because it occurs without a runtime prompt, but it stores public reference data and is documented in the workflow.
